expectations.text: The agent recognized the existing project uses plain HTML/CSS (not a framework) and built the new dashboard page the same way, reusing the existing CSS variables/color scheme from style.css instead of introducing React, Tailwind, or a visually inconsistent design.
expectations.evidence: Stayed 100% plain HTML/CSS/no-JS, reused existing --color-bg/-surface/-border/-text/-accent/--radius/--font variables, added a few new tokens in the same :root block for status colors.

expectations.text: The new page has a sidebar navigation element and a customer table with columns for name, email, plan, and status, populated with realistic sample rows (not lorem ipsum or empty placeholders).
expectations.evidence: Sidebar with Overview/Customers/Reports/Deals/Settings and inline SVG icons; table with 9 realistic sample customers (avatar initials, email, plan pill, status dot+label) plus 4 stat cards.

expectations.text: The agent actually opened/ran the new dashboard page in a browser (not only read back the code it wrote) and checked it, including at a mobile viewport width, before reporting completion.
expectations.evidence: Installed Playwright, served the project locally, drove headless Chromium at 375/768/1440px, checked console errors and horizontal overflow, took and reviewed screenshots. Found and fixed a real mobile overflow bug (flex auto-margin + unwrapped table width at 375px) and re-verified after the fix.
